issues.concern: The English translation 'I looked at my face in the mirror' misrepresents the Japanese '鏡に顔を映した'. The Japanese means 'I reflected my face in the mirror' or 'My face was reflected in the mirror', implying the action of causing the reflection, not merely looking.
issues.suggestion: Change the English translation to 'I reflected my face in the mirror.' or 'My face was reflected in the mirror.'

issues.concern: The English translation 'The camera had captured the moment of the accident' misrepresents the Japanese 'カメラが事故の瞬間を映していた'. '映す' means to project or reflect, not to capture in the sense of recording. While a camera records, the verb '映す' here refers to the image being displayed or shown by the camera, or the camera itself showing the image.
issues.suggestion: Change the English translation to 'The camera was showing the moment of the accident.' or 'The camera was displaying the moment of the accident.'
